name: Shorbat Adas (red lentil soup)
ingredients: 1 tsp paprika (bloomed in 1 tbsp hot olive oil)
preparation: Soften onion, garlic and carrot in oil; add cumin and turmeric.
Add lentils and stock; simmer 20 minutes until collapsed.
Blend smooth or leave rustic; season with salt and lemon juice.
Serve with the paprika oil and coriander.

name: Vegetarian Harira
ingredients: 2 tbsp maida mixed in ¼ cup water (to thicken)
preparation: Soften onion, celery and garlic in oil; add all the spices.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas, lentils and stock; simmer 25 minutes.
Add vermicelli and the maida slurry; simmer 8 minutes, stirring, until silky.
Finish with herbs and lemon juice.

name: Moroccan Chickpea Soup
ingredients: 1 tsp harissa or red chilli paste
preparation: Soften onion and garlic in oil; add spices and harissa.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas and stock; simmer 20 minutes; mash a few chickpeas for body.
Add spinach for the last 2 minutes.
Finish with lemon and coriander.

name: Freekeh Vegetable Soup
preparation: Soften onion, garlic and carrot in oil; add cumin.
Add freekeh and stock; simmer 25 minutes until tender.
Add zucchini for the last 8 minutes.
Season; finish with dried mint, lemon and parsley.

name: Lemony Spinach Lentil Soup
preparation: Soften onion and garlic in oil; add cumin and chilli.
Add lentils and stock; simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in spinach until wilted.
Finish generously with lemon juice, salt and coriander.

name: Falafel
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas (soaked overnight — NOT boiled)
preparation: Grind the soaked (raw) chickpeas with onion, garlic, herbs and spices to a coarse, grainy paste — not a purée.
Mix in baking powder and besan if loose; rest 30 minutes in the fridge.
Shape into balls, roll edges in sesame.
Deep-fry at 175°C until deep brown and crisp; serve with tahini sauce and pita.

name: Cheese Sambousek (eggless)
preparation: Knead maida, salt, olive oil and water into a smooth dough; rest 30 minutes.
Mix cheeses, parsley, mint and nigella.
Roll thin, cut circles, fill, fold into half-moons and press the edges.
Deep-fry until golden, or bake at 200°C for 18 minutes.

name: Spinach Fatayer
ingredients: 400 g spinach (chopped, salted, squeezed very dry)
¼ cup pine nuts or chopped walnuts (optional)
preparation: Make a soft dough with maida, yeast, sugar, salt, water and 2 tbsp oil; rest 1 hour.
Mix spinach, onion, lemon, sumac, remaining oil and nuts.
Roll circles, fill, and pinch into triangles, sealing the seams well.
Bake at 210°C for 15–18 minutes until golden.

name: Batata Harra (spicy potatoes)
preparation: Roast or fry the potato cubes in 3 tbsp oil until golden and crisp.
Sizzle garlic, chilli and spices in the remaining oil 1 minute.
Toss potatoes through with fresh coriander, lemon and salt.

name: Grilled Halloumi with Honey and Za'atar
preparation: Pat halloumi dry; brush with oil.
Grill or pan-sear 2 minutes each side until deeply golden.
Drizzle honey while hot, dust with za'atar and chilli flakes; serve with lemon.

name: Stuffed Vine Leaves (vegetarian dolma)
ingredients: 40 vine leaves (brined, rinsed) or blanched spinach/chard leaves
½ cup fresh parsley and dill (chopped)
preparation: Sauté onion in 3 tbsp oil; add rice, nuts, currants, herbs, cinnamon and salt; cook 3 minutes.
Place a teaspoon on each leaf, fold sides, roll into tight fingers.
Pack seam-down in a pot, add stock, lemon and remaining oil; weight with a plate.
Simmer covered 45 minutes; cool in the pot. Serve at room temperature.

name: Crispy Spiced Chickpeas
preparation: Toss chickpeas in oil and salt; spread on a tray.
Roast at 200°C for 30–35 minutes, shaking twice, until crisp.
Toss with the spices while hot; cool on the tray to stay crunchy.

name: Pumpkin Kibbeh (baked, eggless)
preparation: Knead bulgur, pumpkin, maida, half the spices and salt into the kibbeh shell dough.
Sauté onion in 2 tbsp oil; add spinach, chickpeas, walnuts, remaining spices and pomegranate molasses for the filling.
Press half the dough into an oiled tray, spread filling, top with the rest; score diamonds and drizzle oil.
Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until set and browned.

name: Vegetable Tagine with Chickpeas and Apricots
preparation: Soften onion and garlic in oil; bloom all the spices 1 minute.
Add vegetables, chickpeas, tomatoes, apricots, stock and honey.
Cover and simmer gently 35 minutes without stirring much, tagine-style.
Season; finish with olives, coriander and almonds. Serve with couscous.

name: Imam Bayildi (stuffed eggplant)
preparation: Fry eggplant halves cut-side down in 4 tbsp oil until golden; arrange in a baking dish.
Cook onions slowly in the rest of the oil until sweet; add garlic, tomatoes, sugar, oregano and salt; cook 10 minutes.
Pile the filling onto the eggplants, add water to the dish.
Cover and bake at 180°C for 35 minutes; cool to warm, finish with parsley and lemon. Best not piping hot.

name: Vegetarian Moussaka
ingredients: 2 large eggplants (sliced 1 cm, roasted with 3 tbsp olive oil)
preparation: Make the lentil sauce: soften onion and garlic, add lentils, tomatoes, cinnamon, oregano and salt; simmer 15 minutes.
Make the white sauce: butter, maida, then milk gradually; season with nutmeg and half the cheese.
Layer potatoes, eggplant and lentil sauce; pour the white sauce over, top with cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes; rest 15 minutes before cutting.

name: Mahshi (stuffed capsicums)
ingredients: ½ cup fresh parsley, dill and mint (chopped)
preparation: Mix rice, onion, chopped tomato, herbs, spices, 2 tbsp oil and salt.
Fill capsicums three-quarters full (rice swells); replace the tops.
Stand them in a pot; pour around the blended tomato, stock, lemon and remaining oil.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes until the rice is tender.

name: Kousa Mahshi (stuffed zucchini)
ingredients: 8 medium zucchini (cored with an apple corer)
½ cup fresh parsley and mint
3 cups tomato passata or blended tomatoes
preparation: Mix rice, onion, chopped tomato, herbs, spices, oil and salt; loosely stuff the zucchini.
Lay them in a wide pot; pour over passata and stock with garlic and dried mint.
Simmer covered 40 minutes until zucchini and rice are tender.
Serve with the tomato broth spooned over.

name: Fasolia (white bean stew)
ingredients: 3 cups cooked white beans (cannellini or lima)
preparation: Soften onion, garlic and carrot in oil; add tomato paste and spices, fry 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, beans and stock; simmer 20 minutes until thick and glossy.
Finish with lemon and coriander; serve with vermicelli rice.

name: Bamia (okra and tomato stew)
preparation: Sear okra in 2 tbsp oil until lightly browned; set aside (this keeps it from going slimy).
Soften onion and garlic; add tomato paste and spices.
Add tomatoes, stock and okra; simmer gently 20 minutes without stirring hard.
Finish with lemon and coriander; serve with rice.

name: Cauliflower Shawarma Wraps
ingredients: 3 tbsp tahini mixed with 3 tbsp lemon juice and 3 tbsp water
preparation: Toss florets with oil, all the spices and salt; roast at 220°C for 30 minutes until charred at the edges.
Whisk the tahini-lemon sauce.
Warm the pitas; spread hummus, add cauliflower, vegetables and pickles.
Drizzle tahini sauce, roll and wrap.

name: Paneer Shish-style Skewers
preparation: Whisk curd, oil, lemon, garlic, spices and salt; marinate paneer, capsicum and onion 20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill or pan-sear, turning, 10–12 minutes until charred at the corners; serve with flatbread and tahini sauce.

name: Halloumi and Vegetable Skewers
preparation: Toss halloumi and vegetables in oil, za'atar, oregano and pepper.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill 10–12 minutes, turning, until the cheese is golden.
Whisk lemon and honey; brush over before serving.

name: Falafel Wrap Plate with Tahini
preparation: Whisk tahini, lemon, water, garlic and salt into a pourable sauce.
Warm pitas; spread hummus.
Fill with falafel, vegetables and pickles; drizzle tahini sauce generously; scatter parsley.

name: Maghmour (eggplant and chickpea stew)
ingredients: 2 large eggplants (cubed, salted 15 minutes, patted dry)
preparation: Brown the eggplant in 4 tbsp oil in batches; set aside.
Soften onion and garlic in the rest; add tomatoes, chickpeas, cumin, mint and water; simmer 10 minutes.
Return eggplant; simmer gently 20 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes; serve warm or at room temperature with pita.

name: Spinach and Cheese Borek (eggless)
ingredients: 150 g butter (melted) or ¾ cup olive oil
preparation: Mix spinach, cheeses, sautéed onion, mint and pepper.
Layer 6 filo sheets in a buttered tray, brushing each with butter; spread the filling.
Top with 6 more buttered sheets; score portions, brush with milk, scatter seeds.
Bake at 190°C for 30–35 minutes until deep golden. Rest 10 minutes.

name: Mujadara (lentils, rice and crispy onions)
ingredients: 3 onions (2 thinly sliced for frying, 1 chopped)
preparation: Fry the sliced onions slowly in 4 tbsp oil until deep brown and crisp; drain.
Boil lentils 12 minutes; drain.
Soften the chopped onion in the rest of the oil; add rice, lentils, cumin, cinnamon, stock and salt; cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes; serve piled with crispy onions and a spoon of curd.

name: Koshari (Egyptian rice, lentils and pasta)
ingredients: 1 cup brown lentils (boiled until just tender)
2 onions (thinly sliced, fried crisp in 4 tbsp oil)
preparation: Cook rice in stock; keep the lentils and macaroni ready.
Make the sauce: garlic in oil, then tomatoes, paste, spices, vinegar and salt; simmer 10 minutes.
Layer rice, lentils, macaroni and chickpeas on a platter.
Pour the spiced tomato sauce over and crown with crispy onions.

name: Vegetable Maqluba (upside-down rice)
ingredients: 1 eggplant (thick slices, fried golden in 4 tbsp oil)
1 tsp maqluba spice mix (cinnamon, allspice, cumin — ½ tsp each)
¼ cup toasted almonds and pine nuts
preparation: Soften onion and garlic in oil with the spices.
Layer a deep pot: vegetables on the bottom and sides, then the drained rice and the onion mixture.
Pour hot stock gently down the side; simmer covered 30 minutes until absorbed.
Rest 15 minutes, place a platter on top and flip in one confident motion; scatter nuts and parsley.

name: Ruz bil Shaghria (vermicelli rice)
preparation: Toast the vermicelli in butter, stirring, until deep golden.
Add rice and stir 2 minutes.
Add stock and salt; cover and simmer 15 minutes; rest 10 and fluff.

name: Freekeh Pilaf with Caramelised Onions
preparation: Caramelise the onions slowly in oil, 15 minutes.
Add freekeh, cumin and cinnamon; stir 2 minutes.
Add stock and salt; cover and simmer 25 minutes.
Finish with almonds and parsley.

name: Herbed Bulgur Pilaf
ingredients: ¼ cup fresh parsley and mint
preparation: Soften onion in oil; add tomatoes and paste, cook 3 minutes.
Add bulgur, cumin, stock and salt; cover and simmer 12 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes; fluff with herbs and lemon.

name: Couscous with Seven Vegetables
preparation: Simmer all the vegetables, chickpeas, tomatoes, spices and stew stock 20 minutes.
Pour hot stock over the couscous with 1 tbsp oil; cover 5 minutes and fluff.
Mound couscous, ladle the vegetable stew over, scatter raisins.

name: Jeweled Saffron Rice
ingredients: a generous pinch of saffron (steeped in 3 tbsp hot water)
½ cup mixed dried fruit (apricots, cranberries, raisins — chopped)
preparation: Soften onion in butter with cumin seeds and cinnamon.
Add drained rice, stock and salt; cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes; drizzle the saffron water over one section for colour contrast.
Fluff gently and top with dried fruit and nuts.

name: Loubia bi Zeit (green beans in olive oil)
preparation: Soften onion and garlic in the oil generously.
Add beans and coat well; add tomatoes, cinnamon, water and salt.
Simmer covered 20 minutes until the beans are soft, not crunchy.
Serve warm or at room temperature with lemon.

name: Sabanekh (spinach with pine nuts)
preparation: Soften onion and garlic in oil; add ground coriander.
Add spinach and cook until just wilted and the liquid evaporates.
Season; finish with lemon and toasted pine nuts.

name: Roasted Cauliflower with Tahini
preparation: Toss florets with oil, cumin, paprika and salt; roast at 220°C for 28 minutes until charred at the edges.
Whisk tahini, lemon, garlic, water and salt into a smooth sauce.
Drizzle over the hot cauliflower; finish with parsley and pomegranate.

name: Za'atar Roast Carrots
ingredients: ¼ cup thick curd or labneh (to serve)
preparation: Toss carrots with oil, half the za'atar and salt; roast at 210°C for 25–30 minutes.
Whisk honey and lemon; toss the hot carrots through.
Serve over a swipe of labneh, dusted with the rest of the za'atar and pistachios.

name: Pita Bread
preparation: Knead everything into a soft dough; rest 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 10 balls; roll into 5 mm rounds; rest 15 minutes.
Bake on a preheated tray at 250°C for 3–4 minutes until they balloon, or puff on a very hot pan.

name: Za'atar Manakish
preparation: Make a soft dough; rest 1 hour.
Mix za'atar with the topping oil into a paste.
Roll rounds, dimple with fingertips, spread the za'atar oil.
Bake at 230°C for 8–10 minutes until the edges colour.

name: Cheese Manakish
ingredients: ½ cup crumbled feta (vegetarian rennet) or paneer
preparation: Make a soft dough; rest 1 hour.
Mix the cheeses with nigella and mint.
Roll rounds, top with cheese, press lightly.
Bake at 230°C for 10–12 minutes until bubbling.

name: Hummus
ingredients: 3 cups cooked chickpeas (a few reserved for topping)
preparation: Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic, cumin and salt, streaming in iced water until whipped and pale.
Swirl onto a plate; pool olive oil in the centre.
Top with reserved chickpeas and paprika. Keeps 4 days refrigerated.

name: Baba Ganoush
preparation: Char the eggplants whole over a flame or under a grill until collapsed and smoky, 20–30 minutes.
Scoop the flesh, drain 10 minutes, then mash with tahini, lemon, garlic and salt.
Finish with olive oil, parsley and pomegranate.

name: Tabbouleh
ingredients: 3 cups fresh parsley (finely chopped — the salad is mostly parsley)
¼ cup fine bulgur (soaked in hot water 15 minutes, squeezed)
preparation: Squeeze the soaked bulgur very dry.
Toss with parsley, mint, tomato and spring onion.
Dress with lemon, oil, allspice and salt just before serving.

name: Muhammara (walnut and red pepper dip)
preparation: Blend capsicum, walnuts, breadcrumbs, pomegranate molasses, lemon, garlic and spices coarsely.
Stream in the olive oil; keep some texture.
Rest 30 minutes; serve with pita and a drizzle of oil.

name: Baklava
ingredients: 1 tsp rose water or orange blossom water (optional)
preparation: Layer 10 buttered filo sheets in a tray; spread the cinnamon nuts; layer 10 more buttered sheets.
Cut diamonds all the way through; bake at 170°C for 40–45 minutes until deep golden.
Boil sugar, water, honey and lemon 8 minutes; add rose water; cool slightly.
Pour the syrup over the hot baklava; rest at least 4 hours before serving.

name: Basbousa (semolina cake, eggless)
ingredients: ½ cup melted butter or ghee
preparation: Mix semolina, coconut, sugar, curd, butter, baking powder and soda; rest 15 minutes.
Spread in a greased tray, score diamonds, press an almond on each.
Bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until golden.
Boil the syrup ingredients 5 minutes; pour over the hot cake; rest 1 hour.

name: Kunafa
ingredients: 300 g fresh mozzarella (sliced, soaked in water 10 minutes to desalt)
1 tsp rose water or orange blossom water
a few drops orange food colour (optional)
preparation: Toss the shredded pastry with melted butter until every strand is coated.
Press half into a buttered pan; layer the cheeses; press the rest on top.
Cook on medium-low 10–12 minutes until the base is deep gold, then flip and crisp the other side (or bake at 190°C for 25 minutes).
Boil the syrup 6 minutes with lemon and rose water; pour over the hot kunafa; top with pistachios and serve immediately.

name: Ma'amoul (date-filled cookies, eggless)
ingredients: 1½ cups soft dates (pitted, mashed with 1 tbsp butter and ½ tsp cinnamon)
preparation: Rub butter into semolina, maida and sugar; bind with milk and rose water; rest 30 minutes.
Roll the date paste into small balls.
Wrap dough around each ball; press into a ma'amoul mould or crimp with a fork.
Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until pale gold; cool and dust with icing sugar.

name: Limonana (mint lemonade)
preparation: Blend lemon juice, sugar, mint, water and half the ice until slushy and pale green.
Taste and adjust sugar.
Pour over the remaining ice; garnish with lemon slices and mint.
